provenance.instrument: Jackson Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. 8 of 4-3-1972, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 JA2360, Township of Jackson, Lebanon County (27-201.2 names 'the Township of Jackson, Lebanon County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and lot, yard and height tables are text in Parts 6 to 10. The only attachments are the airport height appendix and two airport surface figures. Floodplain rules are Part 11 of the zoning chapter (Ord. No. 2-2020). New Laws (0)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 Version Information: 'Includes legislation through 04-06-2026. Uploaded on: 06-10-2026.' New Laws (0)
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters, household employee, conversion) find only 'Conversion Apartments' (27-603H, 27-702.9F) and the short-term rental rules

Conversion apartments are a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in A, R-1 and R-2 (27-603H, 27-702.9F, 27-802.13A). 'Any farmhouse or dwelling may be converted to a dwelling for more than one family' in A. In R-1 and R-2 only a dwelling 'existing at the effective date of this Chapter'. The lot area for each family may not fall below two thirds of the district figure, the outside of the building may not change except as other ordinances require, each apartment needs at least 400 sq ft, and the plans go to the Zoning Hearing Board

R-2 permits two-family detached and semidetached dwellings by right (27-802.2). The lot table gives the area 'for every dwelling unit': 4,000 sq ft for a two-family detached dwelling, 50 ft wide (27-803). A two-family detached dwelling has 'one unit over the other' (27-101)

More than one principal structure may stand on a lot in any district if each meets the yards and the subdivision ordinance 'as though it were on an individual lot' (27-1408). Two or more residential buildings on a lot are a land development (27-101). A single-family detached dwelling is a building 'occupied exclusively by one family on an individual lot' (27-101), so whether a second house may share a lot is not settled

An accessory building 'may not house a principal use nor may it stand alone on a lot as a principal building' (27-101). Accessory buildings may not stand in a required front yard. They must be 5 ft from side and rear lines in R-1 and R-2 and 10 ft in other residential and commercial districts, but the same section then says 'In all districts, accessory buildings shall not be less than 10 feet from a side or rear lot line' (27-1402). A building attached to the house must meet the principal yards

Every dwelling unit needs at least 700 sq ft of habitable floor area 'unless otherwise regulated' (27-1411). An existing two-family or multifamily development may be enlarged only with 3,000 sq ft of lot area for each unit (27-1411)

In A, each farm or property may have only a set number of lots or principal uses, counted from its size on January 6, 1997: one under 25 acres, up to seven at 250 acres (27-604A). Permits for a new dwelling on unsubdivided land need an agricultural plan (27-604B)

Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit for one- and two-family dwellings, off-street but not necessarily paved (27-1505.5). Parking may not be within 25 ft of a street right-of-way and may use up to half of the required front yard (27-1504G)

A use the district tables neither permit nor prohibit goes to the Zoning Hearing Board, which decides 'as an administrative review' whether it is similar to the permitted uses (27-406). No building may be altered to 'accommodate or house a greater number of families' contrary to the chapter (27-403B)
Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the usual hardship findings (27-1904). No bar on a use variance was found

Nonconforming lot of record in separate ownership: a permitted principal structure and accessory structures may be built if the yards are met (27-1302.1). 'Nonconformities shall not be used as grounds for adding other structures or additional uses prohibited elsewhere in the same district' (27-1301.1)

Floodplain (Part 11): a permit is needed for any construction anywhere in the township (27-1108). In a floodway no new construction without a DEP permit and an analysis showing no rise. In an AE area without a floodway nothing new within 50 ft landward of the top of bank unless DEP issues a permit (27-1118.1B(2)(b)). A new or substantially improved home's lowest floor must be at or above the regulatory flood elevation (27-1123.1). An accessory structure in the floodplain that is not elevated may not be used for human habitation and is limited to 200 sq ft (27-1123.5)

C permits 'all other uses, including single-family dwellings, which in the opinion of the Zoning Administrator are similar to the above uses' (27-902.18). I permits 'All single-family dwellings' (27-1002.6)
Short-term rentals need a township license and are not allowed in R-2 or R-R (27-1427.2B)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Jackson Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Not read: Parts 2 and 3 in full, Parts 16 to 18, Part 19 except 27-1904, Parts 20 to 28, 27-1128, 27-1137 to 27-1139, 27-1428, 27-1429 and the rest of the 27-101 definitions. 27-501 still lists 'C-1', 'I-1' and F-1 to F-3 floodplain districts and leaves out R-R (added by Ord. No. 2-2021). This file uses the Part titles A, R-R, R-1, R-2, C and I.

status.note: No district lists a second dwelling on a single-family lot as an accessory use. A house may become a dwelling for more than one family by special exception in A, R-1 and R-2

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). A unit inside the house may instead be a conversion apartment by special exception in A, R-1 and R-2, and R-2 permits two-family dwellings by right (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, on the findings of 27-1904. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Conversion apartments (A)
value.conditions: Any farmhouse or dwelling may be converted to a dwelling for more than one family. The lot area for each family may not fall below two thirds of the district figure (one acre for each dwelling unit, 27-605), so two families need 58,080 sq ft. No exterior evidence of change in the building except as other ordinances require. Fire escapes at the rear, not on a wall facing a street. Parking under Part 15. At least 400 sq ft for each apartment. Plans go to the Zoning Hearing Board
value.note: A house turned into two units, not a unit added to it. 58,080 sq ft is two thirds of an acre for each of two families. Whether the conversion counts against the farm's allotment of lots or principal uses (27-604A) is not settled

value.name: Conversion apartments (R-1)
value.conditions: Only a farm house or dwelling 'existing at the effective date of this Chapter'. The lot area for each family may not fall below two thirds of the district figure. No exterior evidence or change in the building except as other ordinances require. Fire escapes at the rear. Parking under Part 15. At least 400 sq ft for each apartment. Plans go to the Zoning Hearing Board

value.condition: In a floodway 'no new construction or development shall be allowed, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office.' No encroachment, new construction or substantial improvement is allowed unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels.

In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection's regional office.' With all other development it may not raise flood levels more than one foot.

In the identified floodplain a new or substantially improved home must have its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. An accessory structure that is not elevated 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may be at most 200 sq ft. No variance for an accessory structure over 600 sq ft.
